prompt: Teams discover the same interface mismatch late in integration. Which investment would shorten the next decision cycle?

options.text: Add a second sign-off meeting before integration.
options.feedback: The team would still discover the mismatch at integration. Identify where the two interface definitions first become comparable.

options.text: Check the two versioned interface definitions whenever either changes.
options.feedback: An early comparison exposes a disagreement while the teams can still change their designs. The reusable check improves the engineering system.

options.text: Build the next product variant before investigating the mismatch.
options.feedback: A further variant increases the number of configurations the teams must investigate. It does little to locate the existing disagreement.

prompt: A model check passes for a proposed design change. Which decision can the team now make?

options.text: Use the result to decide what to integrate or investigate next.
options.feedback: The check gives timely evidence about the modeled condition. The team can use that evidence to choose its next integration or test step.

options.text: Release the product in every intended operating condition.
options.feedback: The check covered a particular model and condition. Release also depends on integration and evidence for the intended use.

options.text: Count the check as a measured reduction in total development cost.
options.feedback: A passing check records a technical result. A cost claim needs a measure of the work or rework it actually saved.
